blocks.title: Key Takeaways
items: Infrastructure is broadly divided into Economic Infrastructure (direct support to production) and Social Infrastructure (human resource development).
Economic infrastructure includes transport, communication, power, banking, and irrigation systems.
Power energy is considered the backbone of modern industrial economy, drawing from thermal, hydro, nuclear, and renewable sources.
Social infrastructure focuses on education, health, housing, and sanitation to build human capital and improve living standards.
Major challenges include inadequate investment, poor maintenance, power shortages, and delays in project execution.
Key government initiatives aimed at infrastructure expansion include NIP, PM Gati Shakti Yojana, Bharatmala, and Sagarmala.

blocks.content: Infrastructure refers to the basic physical and institutional facilities that are necessary for the

smooth functioning of an economy. It forms the foundation on which the entire economic system operates. In simple words, infrastructure means those facilities without which production, distribution, trade and daily life cannot function properly.

Economic infrastructure refers to those facilities which directly help in production and economic activities.
Without economic infrastructure, industries and agriculture cannot grow.
Transport is the most important component of economic infrastructure.
It connects producers with consumers and enables movement of goods and people.

items: Road Transport – Most widely used, flexible and suitable for short distances.
Rail Transport – Cheap and suitable for long-distance transport of heavy goods.
Water Transport – Cheapest means for bulk goods.
Air Transport – Fastest but most expensive.
Pipeline Transport – Used for oil, gas and water.

blocks.content: Social infrastructure refers to facilities that improve the quality of human life and develop human capital.
Education develops skills, knowledge and efficiency of people. It plays a vital role in economic and social development.
Health infrastructure includes hospitals, clinics, doctors and medical services. A healthy population is necessary for productivity and growth.
Housing provides shelter and improves living conditions. The government promotes affordable housing schemes.
Sanitation ensures cleanliness and prevents diseases. Swachh Bharat Mission is a major step in this direction.

items: Economic infrastructure directly boosts production and trade, whereas social infrastructure indirectly impacts economic growth by strengthening human capital.
Power sector is categorized into four main sources: Thermal, Hydroelectric, Nuclear, and Renewable energy.
Bharatmala focuses on road development, Sagarmala targets port-led development, and PM Gati Shakti acts as a multi-modal connectivity master plan.
Irrigation helps reduce agricultural dependence on monsoons and facilitates multiple cropping.

blocks.content: ROLE OF INFRASTRUCTURE IN ECONOMIC DEVELOPMENT
Infrastructure is the foundation of economic development.
A strong infrastructure base is essential for achieving sustainable growth, reducing poverty and improving quality of life.
